idiom_name: Flask view function per URL rule (@app.route)
implementation_notes: In Flask the page controller is a function decorated with its URL: @app.route('/orders') binds one view function to one rule, the function reads request/form, calls domain code and returns rendered markup (render_template) or a redirect; the classic controller class is replaced by the decorated function and shared behaviour by before_request hooks or blueprint-wide decorators. Django is the sibling variant: the same idea is expressed as a view callable referenced from a URLconf, with class-based views (TemplateView/ListView subclasses registered through as_view()) when a page needs structure. Prefer Flask's decorator form for page-scoped applications; use Django's URLconf form when the project is already Django and the pages belong to an app's URL tree.
pitfalls: One view function per rule means a forgotten check is forgotten on that page: declare shared guards explicitly with before_request or a decorator, never by assumption.
request and session are context-local proxies: touching them from a background thread or after the request ends raises, so all page data must be read inside the view.
With a reloader or several workers, module-level caches are per-process, not per-request, so a 'global' model list leaks between users and workers.

variants.name: Django URLconf entry pointing at a class-based view
variants.implementation_notes: Django separates the URL map from the handler: urls.py maps each page with path('orders/', OrdersView.as_view()) and the page controller is a class - a View/TemplateView/ListView subclass whose get_context_data/get/post methods fetch the model data and whose template_name selects the view. This is the closest Python gets to the classic per-page controller object, and mixins such as LoginRequiredMixin replace the shared base controller; prefer it when pages need per-page structure or form handling, while a plain function view stays shorter for one-off pages.
variants.code_sketch:
class OrdersView(LoginRequiredMixin, TemplateView):
    template_name = 'orders.html'

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        ctx['orders'] = order_service.list(self.request.user)   # domain logic
        return ctx

# urls.py: path('orders/', OrdersView.as_view())
pitfalls: as_view() must be called in the URLconf: passing the class itself fails, because Django needs a callable view.
The view instance exists per request but the class is shared: assigning request data to class attributes leaks between users.
Class-based views hide behaviour in the mixin MRO and method order, so overriding get() instead of get_context_data() silently drops the template machinery.
